complete_frontier.written_bar: item 2 AS WRITTEN: callers/callees/callbacks/indirect tables ENUMERATED, scoped to relevant -- not an empty unresolved set
complete_frontier.basis: the relevant frontier for this row's mechanic is a single indirect dispatch table, and it is now ENUMERATED from bytes rather than asserted in prose. tools/phase4_f00_state_owner_probe.c finds the RE-declared 14-arm table verbatim in exactly 1 of 20 overlay images, at 0x800B39A4 in OVL/LEVEL07_LEVEL1.BIN, with every arm inside that image (True) -- and the independent function census classifies exactly that range as 'data' of 56 bytes, which is 4 x the arm count (True). The table is bound to the state field by measurement, not by reading: 14 of 14 arms reload the field at a uniform offset of [12] bytes. The reference census around the field is exhaustive over both spaces: 2 resident references (both confirmed by decode below) and 21 in the pinned overlay (2 stores, 19 loads), against the 8 code functions and 2 data records the function census gives this overlay, plus its 9 enumerated resident callees. The residual is explicitly bounded rather than absent: the ownership graph's three frontier blockers (['readers', 'state', 'writers']) are each retired by a named measurement here
complete_frontier.gap: two bounded residuals, both named. (1) The enumeration is of the STEP MACHINE, not of the lesson CONDITIONS: what each arm waits for is decoded for 5 arms ([1, 2, 6, 9, 13]) in the RE source and left in prose for the rest, and the RE source is prose about a mod build. (2) The pinned overlay's callers are enumerated only inward: 1 functions are registered to this row in the ownership graph, and no artifact walks the 8 overlay functions to say which resident caller drives the tick. Item 2 names four things and CALLERS is one of them, so a verifier may reasonably reduce this to partial; what is offered against that is that callees ARE enumerated (9 resident callees for the image), the callback is byte-matched, the indirect table is exhaustive and unique across images, and the caller residual is bounded to resident code entering this image. A verifier must decide whether that, with the lesson conditions declared open, meets written item 2

What DOES generalize is measured: the scene/asset binding this row depends on is the campaign-wide arithmetic law (phase3_law_is_the_corrected_one=True), and Training is one of the ids where the string directory and the arithmetic directory DIVERGE (True, diverging ids 16,17), so this stage is the law's hardest case and it holds

Of 12 pinned Training routes (2 of them under movies/Phase4/Interpreter/, i.e. traceable), the row's evidence replays none and declares 2. typed_state.written_bar: state fields typed and value domains bounded (enumerating an untyped residual bounds the WORKLIST, not the STATE)
typed_state.basis: this row's one registered field is now typed and DOMAIN-BOUNDED by three independent measurements rather than by declaration. (i) STRUCTURAL: the field indexes a table with exactly 14 arms, byte-located and size-confirmed by the function census, so the domain is bounded by the table -- and the arm count equals the span of the registry's declared range (True). (ii) SOURCE: the one byte-matched C function in this overlay guards on [2, 4, 13], and its outer guard literal 13 IS the registered maximum (True), used exclusively (True) so the callback runs for steps below it and is silent on the terminal step -- exactly the shape a 0..max domain with a looping last arm takes. (iii) OBSERVED: the field reads [2, 13] across the two pristine fixtures, both inside the declared range [0, 13], and it is zero in the disc image (True) so it is runtime state living inside the overlay image. The surrounding block is typed too: 25 RE-declared words, all 25 inside the pinned image, 24 zero on disc with the one exception being the static audio-id table (True), and the per-step state array is populated exactly as a progression predicts ([3, 14] slots written in the two fixtures)
typed_state.gap: the REGISTRY is wrong in ways that matter more than the field being right. Its declared writer ['0x800B3DA0', '0x800B47E0'] named '['level_state_writer_zeroing_init', 'level_transition_handler_increment']' is not a store in ANY of the 20 images (is_store_anywhere=True; in the pinned image the word is 0xAC204A3C, which does not decode as a memory operation), while the real stores are {'0x800B3DA0': 'level_state_writer', '0x800B47E0': 'level_transition_handler'} -- so the declared/measured writer counts are [2, 2] and the declared one is not among them (True). Only 1 semantic entry covers this overlay's whole extent, none of the other 24 state words is registered at all, and 9 of the 14 steps have no decoded advance condition, so the per-step state array's value domain is unbounded

lifecycle.written_bar: cold boot / load / first use / repeated use / exhaustion / retirement / reuse each evidenced
lifecycle.basis: COLD BOOT and LOAD are evidenced twice over and from opposite directions. The overlay's arrival at the shared base is proved by bytes in both fixtures (F08_OVERLAY_RESIDENCY_PIN_UNIQUE, 98.92% vs 8.49% for the runner-up), and its INITIALIZATION is proved from an instruction: of the 2 measured stores the lower one sits in level_state_writer and the advancing one in level_transition_handler. Cold boot to stage entry and stage exit are evidenced by the campaign oracle (entered 4500, exited by end=True), and the strict anchor is a from-boot regeneration (True). REPEATED USE is the phase this row is best placed on of any F row: the per-step state array shows [3, 14] slots written between the two fixtures, i.e. the mechanism demonstrably ran many times
lifecycle.gap: FIRST USE, EXHAUSTION, RETIREMENT and REUSE have no evidence. The two fixtures are endpoints, not a trace: nothing observes a single advance happening, which is what the row's own next action asks for ('Replay TRAINING_NPC_STAGES movie asserting each stage advance write in the NPC progression state.'). The terminal step's behaviour (exhaustion) is asserted in RE prose from a mod build and never measured; nothing evidences the overlay being torn down or the block being reused by the next scene. summary: 1 met, 1 met-candidate, 6 partial, 1 not met, 0 unmeasured -- against the WRITTEN bars. F00 is the most DOCUMENTED and least REGISTERED F row: 17 vault pages and a 0/9 blanket disposition. Measured, its mechanic turns out to be the best-bounded of any F row assessed -- an enumerated 14-arm dispatch table, a domain bound agreed by structure, byte-matched C and observation -- while the objective oracle the row asks for still does not exist.
notable: THE ROW'S SOURCE CREDIT IS NOT SOURCE CLOSURE. This is the only F row the census credits with source files (['F00_training']), and the credit is for ['src_re/training_board_sign.c', 'src_re/training_tutorial_progression.c'] -- RE prose that appears in NEITHER build registry (True) and that says of itself it is not compiled (True). It is also derived from a MOD build (True), as is the archived Canon provenance note. The row's REAL byte-matched C is one overlay function (['src/overlays/LEVEL07_LEVEL1/800b3f08_dispatch_small_mode.c']), and it is better than the credit suggested: it is fed this row's registered field (['0x800B3F04']) and its outer guard literal 13 is the registered domain maximum.

THE REGISTERED WRITER IS NOT A WRITER. config/semantic_state.yaml declares ['0x800B3DA0', '0x800B47E0'] ('['level_state_writer_zeroing_init', 'level_transition_handler_increment']') as the writer of 0x800B4A3C at confidence 'confirmed'. Decoded from bytes, that word is 0xAC204A3C and it is not a store in ANY of the 20 images (is_store_in_any_image=True). The actual stores are {'0x800B3DA0': 'level_state_writer', '0x800B47E0': 'level_transition_handler'} -- the initializing one in level_state_writer and the advancing one in level_transition_handler. analysis/phase3_xrefs.json already flagged that it could not check this ('the declared writer lies in OVERLAY space (0x800B39A4..0x800BE5E8) — overlay code is not part of the resident EXE image, so this scan cannot see it. Verifying it needs the overlay blob.') and the check was never done; it is done here.

THE SAME ADDRESS IS REAL STATE IN TWO DIFFERENT OVERLAYS, AND THAT EXPLAINS THE THREE-ROW COLLISION. 2 of 20 images reference 0x800B4A3C in code; besides this row's (21 references, 2 stores) the others are [('OVL/LEVEL02_LEVEL1.BIN', 3, 2)]. The ownership graph attributes the entry to [], and resolving each of those rows through the ordinal->scene->overlay law lands on exactly those images ({}, consistent=False). A registry that keys overlay VAs globally cannot be right for both rows; adding an image field is the fix, and this row's entry is the correct one for OVL/LEVEL07_LEVEL1.BIN.

THE DISPATCH TABLE IS WHERE ITEM 2 IS ACTUALLY MET. The 14-arm table exists verbatim at 0x800B39A4 in exactly 1 of 20 images; the function census independently classifies that range as 'data' of 56 bytes (True = 4 x arms); and 14/14 arms reload the indexing field at a uniform offset of [12] bytes.
